Claude now joins your calls

12 November 2026 · Reading time: 4 minutes · Audio in the app: 5 minutes. Listening to the briefing is part of Sapaude Pro.

Anthropic has started a beta in which Claude joins video calls as a visible participant, answers questions and writes the notes while the team keeps talking.

Sapaude retells the story in its own words. The source is below. Publisher: Sapaude.

In three points

Three points, in this order: what the source shows, where that claim stops, and what to check next.

  1. Claude Meetings puts Claude on a call as a participant. It answers spoken or typed questions in writing and builds docs and whiteboards that teammates can edit live.
  2. The beta is rolling out on Team and Enterprise plans and works only with Google Meet for now. By default Claude stays out of calls with people from outside the organization.
  3. Notes and transcripts are free during the beta. Answers that use a connected tool count toward plan usage, and Anthropic says everyone on the call should agree to be transcribed.

Claude takes a seat in the meeting

Anthropic has launched Claude Meetings in beta. Claude can now join a video call as a visible participant, follow the conversation and start on the work while people are still talking. Team members can ask it questions out loud or in the chat. By default Claude answers in writing, and it can use connected tools with the permission of the person asking.

During the call Claude builds docs, whiteboards and other artifacts that teammates on the invite can refine at the same time. It also writes the notes and the action items, so nobody on the call has to. Meetings follows Anthropic's recent push to turn the Claude app into a place for office work, after sheets, whiteboards and data views.

A planning call, step by step

Anthropic's own example is a team planning a customer event. Someone says, "Claude, start a doc for this plan." Claude writes up what has been said so far, and the others edit the plan while the conversation continues.

When the budget comes up, someone asks what last year's event cost. Claude asks for approval to look it up, posts the figure in the meeting chat and compares it with the current plan. The timeline goes onto a whiteboard. Before the end, someone asks for a recap. After the call, the notes, action items, plan and whiteboard sit on the meeting's own page in claude.ai, where people can later ask Claude about past meetings or add it to the next one from their calendar.

Anthropic says it is working with partners such as Gong, Granola, Fireflies.ai and Otter so that transcripts can soon be sent to the tools teams already use.

Rules for guests, tools and data

The beta is rolling out on Team and Enterprise plans and supports Google Meet only. Other platforms are coming, Anthropic says. On Team plans, inviting Claude is on by default and an admin can turn it off. On Enterprise plans, an admin switches it on for all or part of the organization. Organizations with zero data retention, a HIPAA-ready configuration or customer-managed encryption keys are excluded for now.

By default Claude stays out of a call when someone from outside the organization is invited, and leaves if an outsider joins partway through. An admin can allow outside guests. Claude then posts its notice but does not reply in the chat, and what guests say still ends up in the notes and the transcript.

When it joins, Claude appears as a participant and posts a notice in the chat. It saves a transcript, a summary and descriptions of the screen, but no audio. It asks each person the first time it wants to use their connected tools, and that yes applies from then on. For spoken requests it asks every time to confirm who is speaking. Anything it posts in the chat is visible to everyone on the call.

What it costs and how to start

During the beta, notes, transcripts and answers are free on Team and Enterprise plans, unless an answer uses a connected tool, which counts toward the plan's usage. Docs, whiteboards and other artifacts made in a call are free until 10 February 2027.

Anthropic asks users to make sure everyone on a call is fine with being transcribed before they add Claude or turn on auto-join. A sensible first test is one internal meeting without outside guests, followed by a look at whether Claude's action items match what was actually agreed.

What you can do

If your team uses Claude Team or Enterprise and Google Meet, ask your admin whether Meetings is on. Agree on transcription with everyone first, then try it in one internal meeting and check its action items against your own notes.

In the app, the same story is also told shorter and in more detail, matched to your level.
